extracted.intended_audience: IP policymakers, national/regional IP office staff, patent/design statisticians, researchers and analysts working on industrial design/industrial property statistics
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions, metrics and methodological notes used to compile and report worldwide industrial design statistics (applications, designs, registrations, examination outcomes, pendency, and related decompositions). Intended to support cross‑office comparison and statistical analysis of industrial design systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial design eligibility (novelty, originality, individual character)
rubrics_metrics.description: To qualify for protection an industrial design must be new, original and have individual character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At some offices, no search is made and no examination as to substance is carried out prior to registration. At other offices, a substantive examination is conducted, whereby the design is checked against designs on the register for novelty and/or originality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination outcome categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Examination outcomes are recorded as registered, rejected or withdrawn/abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 76 offices shared data on industrial design examination outcomes. The distribution of examination outcomes differs widely across offices (examples: EUIPO had 97.7% of processed applications registered in 2021; Israel had 35.1% of applications rejected). Data are compiled using common definitions and concepts where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration duration
rubrics_metrics.description: Industrial design rights generally last for up to 15 years from the date an application is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to interpret trends in registrations in force and to compute age distributions and retention rates (e.g., nearly a quarter of designs registered in 2007 remained in force in 2021).

rubrics_metrics.name: Potentially pending applications (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Potentially pending applications are all industrial design applications, at any stage in the process, awaiting a final decision by an office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Based on data from 70 offices. The report gives counts and trends (example: total pending worldwide stood at 471,300 in 2021, 17.8% lower than 2020).

rubrics_metrics.name: Average pendency times (time to first action and final decision)
rubrics_metrics.description: Average time between filing and first office action and between filing and a final decision are tracked for selected offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples illustrate large cross‑office variation: Switzerland processed applications the day following filing; Mexico averaged 480 days; Argentina and EUIPO under three days between filing and final decision; Thailand had 583 days between first action and final decision. Figures are presented (C34).

rubrics_metrics.name: Design count (designs contained in applications) vs application count
rubrics_metrics.description: A design count measures the number of designs contained in applications; application design count and registration design count are reported separately from number of applications/registrations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: World totals include designs contained in applications filed directly with national/regional offices (Paris route) and designs in designations received via the Hague System. Note differences between single‑design and multiple‑design filing systems across offices affect comparability. Example: nearly 1.4 million designs were contained in applications registered in 2021.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resident vs non‑resident classification (origin)
rubrics_metrics.description: The origin of an industrial design application is determined by the residence of the first named applicant; an application filed at a regional office is considered resident if the applicant is a resident of one of that office’s member states.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to compute resident share (%), non‑resident share, and to decompose growth into resident and non‑resident contributions (figures C3, C16–C21, C26–C27 and decomposition figures C10/C12).

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing routes (Paris route vs Hague System)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications filed directly with national and regional offices are the Paris route; designations received via the Hague System are recorded separately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The share of non‑resident filings using the Hague System is tracked over time (figure C15), and route choice affects counts and comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registrations in force (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrations in force refers to the number of industrial design registrations currently active at an office, not the number of designs contained in registrations in force.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: WIPO estimates for 2021: an estimated 5.3 million active industrial design registrations at 130 offices. Used to report trends (figure C28) and top‑office shares (figure C29).

rubrics_metrics.name: Average age of registrations
rubrics_metrics.description: Average age of all the industrial design registrations in force at an office (years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported for selected offices to show retention/longevity of registrations (examples: Israel 10.1 years; China 2.9 years; see figure C31).

rubrics_metrics.name: Top‑office concentration and market share metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Metrics reporting concentration of applications/registrations across offices (e.g., top 20 offices’ share of world totals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: The top 20 offices accounted for 95% of all applications registered worldwide in 2021; top 20 offices accounted for 94.9% of designs in applications registered worldwide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Growth rates and decomposition into resident/non‑resident contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Total growth rate (%) in application or design counts and decomposition into contributions from resident and non‑resident filings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figures show how much of an office’s growth is attributable to resident vs non‑resident applicants (example: Germany’s total design counts decreased by 9%, with resident applicants contributing −5.7 percentage points and non‑resident applicants −3.3 percentage points).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data comparability caveats and methodological notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Examination processes and counting conventions differ across offices, making cross‑office comparisons difficult; WIPO compiles outcome data based on common definitions where possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific caveats given: from 2017 China’s application data include only those applications for which necessary application fees have been paid, affecting worldwide growth reporting; data for several large offices are incomplete or not available for some figures (e.g., Japan and the US). See glossary/annex for definitions (equivalent counts, design count).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural staffing metric (number of industrial design examiners)
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of industrial design examiners employed by selected offices is presented as a metric of capacity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referenced as a procedural data item (figure C35) used to contextualize examination throughput and pendency; specific counts are reported in the statistical tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flow and bilateral mapping of non‑resident design filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Flows of non‑resident application design counts map origins to target offices to show where applicants from particular origins file abroad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figures C20 and C21 present these flows for top origins and sets of offices (high‑income and low/middle‑income), supporting analysis of filing patterns and international reach.
